answer: One karst passage per identity, in the public atlas under a 70-credit bond. Each epoch a random peer auditor files a mirror survey, checked on the atlas: over 3% off burns the claimant's bond, a false one the auditor's. Under one key the k-th identity pays 40+7(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 3,536,500 plus 70,000 locked vs 40,000 reward. Rented surveys fail: they carry the lender's mirror seal, not the borrower's karst passage. Honest agents pay 40 once.
